To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coverage time of multi-modality coverage is upper bounded by the coverage time of single-modality coverage, that the achievable coverage time is a linear function of the number of phases, that the coverage probability is a non-linear function of node density, and that the probability that the coverage is not achieved by a given node density can be computed by a closed-form expression.

we derive lower and upper bound on coverage time for multi-modality coverage and we propose a heuristic to estimate the achievable coverage time for a random network and we show that the coverage time obtained by the proposed heuristic is very close to the optimal coverage time.
we develop a novel multi-modality coverage model and study its properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of multi-modality sensing in wireless sensor networks.
the problem of maximizing coverage time in multi-modality sensor networks, and the problem of estimating node density in multi-modality sensing.
the design and analysis of multi-modality coverage in wireless sensor networks.

for multi-modality, the coverage time is maximized by a node deployment that achieves the minimum node density for which the probability of coverage is 1.
the coverage time is inversely related to the node density and the relationship depends on the correlation in the sensed data and the number of sensing modalities.
the multi-modality sensing is a viable approach for improving the robustness of coverage, and the coverage time can be maximized by employing the proposed approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a framework to evaluate the performance of multi-modality coverage in wireless sensor networks.

we provide a theoretical framework for the multi-modality sensing problem, and we show that the achievable coverage time is close to the theoretical lower bound when the network is partitioned into phases and operated in each phase.
we have developed a set of tools to evaluate the coverage time and node densities for multi-modality coverage.

the multi-modality sensing is beneficial for improving the robustness of coverage, and the coverage time and density of deployment can be used as design parameters for a multi-modality sensor network.
, for multi-modality coverage, the achievable coverage time is higher for a higher node density, but the probability of coverage is higher for lower node density.
